lessons.title: Arrays
lessons.metaTitle: Arrays: operations, storage, and interview patterns
lessons.metaDescription: Understand array indexing, insertion, iteration, and resizing, then practice the invariants used in array and matrix interview problems.

lessons.title: Implement an Array
lessons.metaTitle: Implement an array data structure
lessons.metaDescription: Build an array abstraction and reason about indexed access, insertion, removal, capacity, and the costs of moving existing elements.

lessons.title: Walk a Matrix
lessons.metaTitle: Walk a matrix: two-dimensional array traversal
lessons.metaDescription: Practice traversing a two-dimensional matrix while tracking row and column boundaries and handling small or empty inputs.

lessons.title: Product Array
lessons.metaTitle: Product of Array Except Self: prefix and suffix products
lessons.metaDescription: Compute each array position from the product of the other values without division. Work through prefix/suffix state and zero-value cases.

lessons.title: Valid Sudoku Board
lessons.metaTitle: Validate a Sudoku board with sets
lessons.metaDescription: Check Sudoku rows, columns, and subgrids for duplicate values. Practice mapping board positions to the constraints they must satisfy.

lessons.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
lessons.metaTitle: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock: one-pass reasoning
lessons.metaDescription: Find the best single buy-and-sell opportunity by tracking an earlier minimum. Practice ordering constraints and decreasing-price inputs.

lessons.title: How to Succeed in this Course
Big O Notation Time and Space Complexity
lessons.metaTitle: Big O notation: time and space complexity
lessons.metaDescription: Analyze how interview solutions grow with input size. Compare loops, recursion, auxiliary memory, and common complexity classes.

lessons.title: Hash Tables
lessons.metaTitle: Hash tables: lookups, collisions, and frequency counts
lessons.metaDescription: Learn how hashing maps keys to storage, why collisions matter, and how maps and sets support common interview optimizations.

lessons.title: Implement a Hash Table
lessons.metaTitle: Implement a hash table and handle collisions
lessons.metaDescription: Build a hash-table implementation, store and retrieve key/value pairs, and examine how collisions affect correctness and performance.

lessons.title: Catch the Hacker
lessons.metaTitle: Find the most frequent value with a hash map
lessons.metaDescription: Identify a repeatedly duplicated email by counting frequencies. Compare repeated scans with a map-based pass through the input.

lessons.title: Target Two Sum
lessons.metaTitle: Two Sum: complement lookup and distinct indices
lessons.metaDescription: Find two distinct indices whose values reach a target. Compare pair enumeration with a hash-map solution and test duplicate values.
lessons.description: Two sum is one of the most common interview questions and is essential know it completely. It also introduces a common optimization technique frequently used.

lessons.title: Strings
lessons.metaTitle: Strings for interviews: representation and operations
lessons.metaDescription: Study string traversal, character representation, immutability, and construction costs before practicing text interview problems.

lessons.title: Palindromes, Permutations, Anagrams
lessons.metaTitle: Palindromes, permutations, and anagrams explained
lessons.metaDescription: Distinguish palindrome order, permutation arrangements, and anagram frequency counts, then choose the state each text problem needs.

lessons.title: Group Permutations of Palindromes
lessons.metaTitle: Group permutations of palindromes
lessons.metaDescription: Practice grouping strings by character relationships and reasoning about which arrangements can form a palindrome.

lessons.title: Recursion
lessons.metaTitle: Recursion: base cases, call stacks, and return values
lessons.metaDescription: Trace recursive execution, define a smaller subproblem, and connect base cases and return values to a clear correctness argument.

lessons.title: Sum Digits
lessons.metaTitle: Sum the digits of a number without converting to a string
lessons.metaDescription: Compute a number’s digit sum using arithmetic. Practice recursive decomposition, termination, and tests for single-digit inputs.

lessons.title: Generate All Permutations
lessons.metaTitle: Generate all permutations with backtracking
lessons.metaDescription: Enumerate input arrangements while managing choices and restoring state. Analyze the output size and test small permutation examples.

lessons.title: Logarithms and Time Complexity
lessons.metaTitle: Logarithms and logarithmic time complexity
lessons.metaDescription: Understand why repeated halving produces logarithmic work and apply that reasoning to search intervals and recursive algorithms.

lessons.title: Searching and Binary Search
lessons.metaTitle: Binary search: sorted input and interval invariants
lessons.metaDescription: Search sorted data by narrowing a candidate interval. Practice boundaries, midpoint updates, and the conditions that guarantee progress.

lessons.title: Sorting
lessons.metaTitle: Sorting algorithms and interview tradeoffs
lessons.metaDescription: Compare sorting approaches, runtime assumptions, and the ways sorted order changes an interview problem’s available solutions.

lessons.title: Interview Scheduler
lessons.metaTitle: Interview Scheduler: searching for an available time
lessons.metaDescription: Work through an interview scheduling problem and practice using ordered information to reduce the search for a valid answer.

lessons.title: Shifted Search
lessons.metaTitle: Search a rotated sorted array
lessons.metaDescription: Find a target in a shifted sorted array by reasoning about ordered intervals and choosing which half can still contain the answer.

lessons.title: Sorted Matrix Search
lessons.metaTitle: Search a sorted matrix
lessons.metaDescription: Use a matrix’s ordering constraints to reduce the search space. Track boundaries and test targets at edges or outside the data.

lessons.title: Age Sort
lessons.metaTitle: Age Sort: use bounded values to organize an array
lessons.metaDescription: Explore how a restricted value range can change a sorting problem. Compare counting-based work with general comparison sorting.

lessons.title: First Bad Version
lessons.metaTitle: First Bad Version: binary search on a boundary
lessons.metaDescription: Find a transition in an ordered sequence using a predicate. Practice binary-search interval definitions and edge-boundary cases.

lessons.title: Linked Lists
lessons.metaTitle: Linked lists: nodes, links, and traversal
lessons.metaDescription: Understand linked-list structure, traversal costs, and the pointer relationships behind insertion, deletion, and reversal.

lessons.title: Pointers
lessons.metaTitle: Pointers and references in linked structures
lessons.metaDescription: Reason about references, node identity, and reachability so pointer updates do not lose the remainder of a list or tree.

lessons.title: Implement a Linked List
lessons.metaTitle: Implement a linked list
lessons.metaDescription: Build linked nodes and list operations, maintain head and tail relationships, and test empty and single-node structures.

lessons.title: Combine Blockchains
lessons.metaTitle: Combine Blockchains: work with linked chains
lessons.metaDescription: Practice combining linked chains while preserving their nodes and maintaining the relationships needed to traverse the result.

lessons.title: Reverse a Linked List
lessons.metaTitle: Reverse a linked list: preserve and redirect pointers
lessons.metaDescription: Reverse a list by tracking the previous, current, and next nodes. Explain the invariant and handle empty and single-node inputs.

lessons.title: Mirror Delete
lessons.metaTitle: Mirror Delete: linked-list removal practice
lessons.metaDescription: Work through a linked-list deletion exercise with careful reference updates, boundary checks, and tests that preserve reachable nodes.

lessons.title: Queues
lessons.metaTitle: Queues: first-in-first-out processing
lessons.metaDescription: Learn queue operations, implementation choices, and the role of first-in-first-out order in breadth-first traversal and scheduling.

lessons.title: Stacks
lessons.metaTitle: Stacks: last-in-first-out processing
lessons.metaDescription: Learn stack operations and use last-in-first-out state for nested structures, traversal, and interview problem solving.

lessons.title: Implement a Queue
lessons.metaTitle: Implement a queue data structure
lessons.metaDescription: Implement enqueue and dequeue behavior while maintaining first-in-first-out order and handling empty-queue transitions.

lessons.title: Implement a Stack
lessons.metaTitle: Implement a stack data structure
lessons.metaDescription: Implement push, pop, and peek, maintain the top of the stack, and reason about operation costs and empty-state behavior.

lessons.title: Max Min Stack
lessons.metaTitle: Min and max stack: retain aggregate state
lessons.metaDescription: Support stack operations while tracking minimum and maximum values. Practice duplicate values and restoring earlier aggregate state.

lessons.title: Valid Brackets
lessons.metaTitle: Valid brackets: match nested delimiters with a stack
lessons.metaDescription: Validate bracket ordering with a stack of unmatched openings. Test mismatched types, unfinished openings, and closing-first inputs.

lessons.title: Trees
lessons.metaTitle: Trees: structure, height, and recursive reasoning
lessons.metaDescription: Learn tree terminology and recursive structure, then prepare for traversal, depth, ancestor, and binary-search-tree exercises.

lessons.title: Tree Traversal: In-Order, Pre-Order, Post-Order
lessons.metaTitle: Binary tree traversal: inorder, preorder, and postorder
lessons.metaDescription: Compare traversal orders by changing when each node is processed. Trace recursive calls and distinguish traversal from search-tree ordering.

lessons.title: Binary Search Trees
lessons.metaTitle: Binary search trees: ordering and search
lessons.metaDescription: Understand the ordering rules that guide binary-search-tree operations and how tree height affects search performance.

lessons.title: Implement a Binary Search Tree
lessons.metaTitle: Implement a binary search tree
lessons.metaDescription: Build a binary search tree, preserve its ordering contract during updates, and test search paths and empty-tree behavior.

lessons.title: Binary Tree Max Depth
lessons.metaTitle: Maximum depth of a binary tree
lessons.metaDescription: Compute a tree’s depth from its subtrees. State the empty-tree convention and compare balanced and chain-shaped inputs.

lessons.title: BST Validate
lessons.metaTitle: Validate a binary search tree with ancestor bounds
lessons.metaDescription: Check the complete binary-search-tree ordering rule, including ancestor constraints that a parent-only comparison can miss.

lessons.title: Closest Common Ancestor in Binary Tree
lessons.metaTitle: Lowest common ancestor of a binary tree
lessons.metaDescription: Find the shared ancestor of two nodes by reasoning about subtree results and the relationship between node identity and ancestry.

lessons.title: Graphs
lessons.metaTitle: Graphs: representations, traversal, and interview problems
lessons.metaDescription: Model relationships with graph nodes and edges, compare representations, and prepare for reachability and traversal exercises.

lessons.title: Depth-First Search
lessons.metaTitle: Depth-first search: visited state and active paths
lessons.metaDescription: Traverse a graph by following branches, track visited nodes to handle cycles, and reason about recursive or explicit stack state.

lessons.title: Breadth-First Search
lessons.metaTitle: Breadth-first search: queues and shortest unweighted paths
lessons.metaDescription: Traverse by distance with a queue, avoid duplicate discoveries, and reconstruct shortest paths when edges have equal cost.

lessons.title: Implement a Graph
lessons.metaTitle: Implement a graph data structure
lessons.metaDescription: Represent vertices and edges, maintain neighbor relationships, and prepare a graph structure for traversal and reachability queries.

lessons.title: Pilot a Rocket
lessons.metaTitle: Shortest path in an unweighted graph: Pilot a Rocket
lessons.metaDescription: Find a route through a satellite network. Practice BFS discovery order, parent tracking, cycles, and an unreachable destination.

lessons.title: Count Islands
lessons.metaTitle: Number of Islands: DFS and BFS region counting
lessons.metaDescription: Count connected land regions in a matrix. Compare DFS and BFS, mark visited cells, and test disconnected and diagonal land.

lessons.title: Robot Maze
lessons.metaTitle: Robot Maze: find a valid path through a grid
lessons.metaDescription: Determine whether a robot can reach an exit under the allowed movement rules. Practice grid bounds, blocked cells, and path choices.

lessons.title: Subproblems and Overlapping Subproblems
lessons.metaTitle: Subproblems and overlapping subproblems
lessons.metaDescription: Identify repeated smaller decisions and define state precisely before using caching or a dynamic-programming table.

lessons.title: Memoization
lessons.metaTitle: Memoization: cache repeated subproblem results
lessons.metaDescription: Turn repeated recursive work into reusable results. Choose complete cache keys and distinguish missing results from valid zero values.

lessons.title: Bottom-Up vs. Top-Down
lessons.metaTitle: Top-down vs. bottom-up dynamic programming
lessons.metaDescription: Compare memoized recursion with tabulation, choose a valid evaluation order, and reason about stack and table storage.

lessons.title: Dynamic Programming
lessons.metaTitle: Dynamic programming: states, transitions, and subproblems
lessons.metaDescription: Develop a recurrence, identify repeated states, and connect memoization and tabulation to interview problem-solving strategies.

lessons.title: Vending Machine
lessons.metaTitle: Vending Machine: dynamic programming practice
lessons.metaDescription: Work through a vending-machine interview problem by identifying choices, smaller subproblems, and the state needed to reuse results.

lessons.title: Three Moves
lessons.metaTitle: Three Moves: dynamic programming practice
lessons.metaDescription: Define transitions for a constrained-movement problem and practice solving repeated subproblems without recomputing each path.

lessons.title: Steal Packages
lessons.metaTitle: House Robber: choose non-adjacent values with dynamic programming
lessons.metaDescription: Maximize a total without taking adjacent entries. Derive skip/take decisions and compare recursive, memoized, and iterative approaches.

lessons.title: Why does JavaScript Get its Own Topic
lessons.metaTitle: Why JavaScript interview preparation needs language practice
lessons.metaDescription: Connect general algorithm skills with JavaScript-specific behavior, browser programming, and practical utility implementations.

lessons.title: JavaScript Interview Questions
lessons.metaTitle: JavaScript interview questions and language concepts
lessons.metaDescription: Practice explaining JavaScript behavior and implementation choices alongside algorithm exercises and practical coding questions.

lessons.title: Fix 'this'
lessons.metaTitle: JavaScript this binding: fix the receiver
lessons.metaDescription: Trace JavaScript receivers and callback invocation so you can explain and repair unexpected this values in interview code.

lessons.title: Array Methods
lessons.metaTitle: Implement JavaScript array methods
lessons.metaDescription: Practice array-method behavior, callback arguments, iteration, and edge cases by implementing familiar JavaScript operations.

lessons.title: Build a JavaScript Promise
lessons.metaTitle: Build a JavaScript Promise implementation
lessons.metaDescription: Explore asynchronous state, fulfillment, rejection, and chaining by building a teaching implementation of promise behavior.

lessons.title: Pub-Sub and Event-Driven Programming
lessons.metaTitle: Build a JavaScript pub-sub and event emitter
lessons.metaDescription: Implement event subscription and publication, track listeners, and connect the pattern to event-driven JavaScript applications.

lessons.title: Debounce
lessons.metaTitle: Debounce in JavaScript: implementation and timing
lessons.metaDescription: Implement a debounce that waits for activity to settle. Trace timers, preserve arguments and this, and compare it with throttling.

lessons.title: Throttle
lessons.metaTitle: Throttle in JavaScript: implementation and timing
lessons.metaDescription: Limit callback frequency during repeated events. Explain cooldown windows, trailing updates, and how throttling differs from debounce.
